title: Totally True History (Mostly)
blurb: Kings, presidents, inventors and candy bars. Three facts per card, and one is cap.

cards.say: [The first basketball game was played with a soccer ball], [Benjamin Franklin asked Congress to make the turkey the national bird], [Abraham Lincoln is honored in the National Wrestling Hall of Fame], and [a sheep, a duck and a rooster were the first passengers in a hot air balloon].
cards.real: Franklin praised the turkey in a letter to his daughter, but he never asked for it to become a national symbol.

cards.say: [The Statue of Liberty was used as a lighthouse for 16 years], [the teddy bear was invented by a candy shop owner in Brooklyn], [Uranus was almost named George's Star, after Britain's King George III], and [Viking warriors wore metal helmets with big horns sticking out].
cards.real: There's no evidence Vikings wore horned helmets. That look comes from opera costumes made in the 1870s.

cards.say: [Knights in heavy armor had to be lifted onto their horses with cranes], [Benjamin Harrison and his wife were too scared to touch the White House light switches], [King Henry VIII had a bathroom with seats for 28 people at once], and [Pluto was named by an 11-year-old girl from England].
cards.real: Knights climbed onto their horses by themselves. A full suit of plate armor weighed about 45 to 55 pounds.

cards.say: [Barbie's full name is Barbara Millicent Roberts], [a flock of sheep once trimmed the White House lawn], [basketball was invented by an American gym teacher in New York], and [the Palace of Versailles started out as a hunting lodge].
cards.real: Basketball's inventor, James Naismith, was Canadian. He came up with the game in Springfield, Massachusetts, in 1891.

cards.say: [Napoleon was much shorter than most men of his time], [Ken and Barbie were named after their inventor's real children], [people had toilets washed out by running water at least 5,000 years ago], and [merchants were writing the @ sign almost 500 years ago].
cards.real: Napoleon was about 5 feet 6 inches, above average for his time. Old French inches were longer, which confused people.

cards.say: [The first person to go up in a hot air balloon, in 1783, was tied down with a rope], [Hershey's chocolate bars sold for five cents each until the year 1999], [the Goo Goo Cluster, from 1912, was named after a baby's first words], and [the man who built the Eiffel Tower also designed the Statue of Liberty's insides].
cards.real: A Hershey's bar cost five cents from 1900 until 1969, when the price went up.

cards.say: [Caroline Herschel, an astronomer in the 1700s, discovered eight comets], [Alan Turing wrote a chess program in 1948 that no computer back then could run], [basketball's inventor tossed up the first jump ball at the 1936 Olympics], and [the teddy bear, first made in 1902, was named after Franklin Roosevelt].
cards.real: The teddy bear was named after President Theodore Roosevelt, whose nickname was Teddy.

cards.say: [Nintendo's founder was 29 years old when he started the company], [Toblerone's name mixes its maker's family name with an Italian word for nougat], [you can see the Great Wall of China from the Moon with your own eyes], and [Herbert Hoover, in 1929, was the first president with a phone on his desk].
cards.real: The Great Wall is far too narrow to see from the Moon. Even from low orbit, astronauts can barely spot it, if at all.

cards.say: [Cadbury Dairy Milk chocolate was almost named Dairy Maid], [the Statue of Liberty's sandals would be about a size 879], [the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles has 578 mirrors], and [ancient Romans built special rooms for throwing up at big feasts].
cards.real: A vomitorium was really a passageway that let crowds pour in and out of a Roman stadium.

cards.say: [The world's first underground railway opened in New York City], [a toilet hidden inside a fake book was made in France in the 1700s], [the man who designed the Game Boy started out fixing machines in Nintendo's card factory], and [James Garfield gave a campaign speech in German before he became president].
cards.real: The world's first underground railway opened in London in 1863.

cards.say: [Japan banned playing cards from other countries in the 1600s], [Barbie was invented after her creator saw how much her daughter loved paper dolls], [the very first solid chocolate bar was made at a factory in America], and [the man who discovered Uranus was a musician before he was an astronomer].
cards.real: The first solid chocolate bar was made in England by Joseph Fry in 1847.

cards.say: [The man who created Pokémon was nicknamed Dr. Bug as a kid], [a recording of Abraham Lincoln's voice still exists today], [the inventor of basketball had a losing record as a college coach], and [the first free balloon flight with people ended early because the balloon caught fire].
cards.real: No recording of Lincoln exists. The oldest recorded voice of any president belongs to Benjamin Harrison.
